input: I buy ambitious groceries, then order takeaway while they wilt in the fridge.

response.answer:
The Fridge-to-Door Dispatcher
Fictional patent sketch.

FIGURE 1
```text
[A: gleaming produce bin — accepts ambitious groceries]
                   ↓
[B: wilting-leaf timer — tracks edible decay]
                   ↓
[C: takeaway menu projector — displays tempting alternatives]
BACK TO A: the projector's glow re-attracts the operator to the bin's contents
```

CLAIM 1 — An apparatus for converting potential meals into culinary regret, while maintaining the illusion of future healthy eating.

BENCH TEST — In this imagined kitchen, the operator places a head of radicchio and a bunch of asparagus into the gleaming produce bin. The wilting-leaf timer begins its silent count. As the timer nears its third day, the takeaway menu projector activates, casting a warm, inviting glow of pizza and pad thai onto the bin's lid. The operator, drawn by the projector's display, reaches for their phone to order.

REMOVE ONE PART
A: Lose the gleaming produce bin; the groceries have nowhere to go, but the operator must confront them directly.
B: Lose the wilting-leaf timer; the decay is no longer tracked, but the operator might forget the food entirely.
C: Lose the takeaway menu projector; the tempting alternatives vanish, but the operator must remember them independently.

Try outside the sketch: before buying new groceries, write down one meal you intend to make with them.

Choose a part and paste this sketch to request a revision.
